blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Synthetic text generation offers a promising approach to alleviating data scarcity in low-resource languages. However, its effectiveness is inherently limited for languages that are scarcely represented, or entirely absent, in an LLM's pretraining data. At the same time, many such languages have human-curated vocabularies that provide rich lexical and semantic information, often accompanied by grammatical information such as part-of-speech labels. In this work, we ask whether LLMs can leverage these resources to generate coherent text in extremely low-resource and unseen languages. We introduce a framework that combines human-curated vocabularies with a small number of human-written exemplars that provide syntactic signals, while sampling candidate words according to a Zipfian distribution. Across languages with varying levels of resource availability, we evaluate the generated text using lexical diversity, off-target ratio, and human judgments of fluency. Our results show that reasoning-enabled LLMs can generate fluent text even in extremely low-resource languages, with particularly strong results at the sentence level and promising performance at the paragraph level. Our findings highlight a practical pathway for bootstrapping synthetic data in low-resource languages, expanding the amount of usable text even when existing digital resources are extremely limited. Our source code is available at https://github.com/michaelsinanta/vocab2text.
blocks.zh: 合成文本生成为缓解低资源语言的数据稀缺提供了一个很有希望的方法。 然而,对于在LLM预训数据中几乎没有代表或完全没有代表的语言来说,其有效性本来就是有限的. 同时,许多此类语言都有人语化词汇,提供丰富的词汇和语义信息,并经常伴有语法信息,如部分语法标签等. 在这项工作中,我们询问法学硕士是否能够利用这些资源,以极其低的资源和看不见的语言生成一致的文本。 我们引入了一个框架,将人语精准词汇与少量提供综合信号的人类写作实例结合起来,同时根据Zipfian的分布来取样候选词. 在资源提供水平不同的语文中,我们利用词汇多样性、非目标比率以及人对流利性的判断来评价生成的文本。 我们的结果表明,推理驱动的LLMS即使使用极低的资源语言也能产生流利的文字,在句子层面特别有强效的结果,在段落层面有希望的表现. 我们的研究结果突出表明,即使现有数字资源极为有限,也要以低资源语言提供合成数据,扩大可用文本的数量。 我们的源代码见https://github.com/michaelsinanta/vocab2text。

blocks.en: More than 7,000 languages are spoken worldwide, yet only a small fraction are represented in the textual resources commonly used to train language models. For example, Wikipedia and Common Crawl contain textual data for only about 4% of the world’s languages, while human-curated lexicons and word lists cover approximately 70% ( Wang et al., 2022 ) . This broader coverage reflects longstanding language documentation efforts, through which linguists and language communities have compiled human-curated vocabularies that record words, their meanings, and other linguistic information. Their broad coverage creates an opportunity to leverage these existing resources to expand text resources for low-resource languages.
blocks.zh: 全世界有7 000多种语言,但用于培训语言模型的文字资源只占一小部分。 例如,维基百科和Common Crawl只包含世界约4%语言的文字数据,而人类精密词汇和单词列表则涵盖约70%(Wang等人,2022年). 这一更广泛的覆盖面反映了语言文献的长期工作,语言学家和语言界通过这项工作汇编了人语词汇,记录了文字、其含义和其他语言信息。 其广泛的覆盖面为利用现有资源扩大低资源语言的文本资源创造了机会。

blocks.en: One promising way to realize this opportunity is through synthetic text generation. LLMs are increasingly used to generate synthetic data for pretraining and post-training ( Wang et al., 2023 ; Doshi et al., 2024 ; Anikina et al., 2025 ; Stenlund et al., 2026 ) . However, such generation largely relies on the linguistic knowledge already encoded in LLMs, limiting its effectiveness for languages that are poorly represented in their pretraining data ( Guo et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025 ) . Human-curated vocabularies offer a complementary source of linguistic knowledge, yet their potential for LLM-based synthetic text generation remains largely unexplored ( Yong et al., 2024 ) . This idea has a natural parallel in human language learning: when learning an unfamiliar language, people consult dictionaries to acquire new words and use examples to learn how those words appear in context. Inspired by this process, we ask: Can LLMs leverage human-curated vocabularies to generate coherent and lexically diverse text in low-resource languages, including extremely underrepresented languages?
blocks.zh: 实现这一机会的一个有希望的方法是通过合成文本生成。 LLMs越来越多地用于生成供培训前和培训后使用的合成数据(Wang等人,2023年;Doshi等人,2024年;Anikina等人,2025年;Stenlund等人,2026年)。 然而,这种一代主要依靠已经编码为LLMS的语言知识,限制了其在预培训数据中代表性不足的语言的效用(Guo等人,2024年;Li等人,2025年)。 人类精密词汇提供了语言知识的补充来源,但其基于LLM的合成文本生成的潜力基本上仍未加以探讨(Yong等人,2024年)。 这个想法在人类语言学习中有着自然的平行性:在学习一种不熟悉的语言时,人们会参考词典来获取新词,并使用实例来学习这些词在语境中是如何出现的. 受这一进程的启发,我们问:LLMS能否利用人文词汇,以低资源语言,包括代表人数极少的语言,生成连贯和符合语言特点的文字?

blocks.en: Our contributions are threefold: 1. We introduce a training-free framework that leverages LLM reasoning to generate text in low-resource languages from human-curated vocabularies and a small number of human-written exemplars. Our framework adapts from Zipfian sampling to expose the model to a broad yet natural distribution of vocabulary during generation. 2. Across six languages spanning different levels of resource availability, our framework consistently improves lexical diversity and reduces off-target generation over practical baselines. Human evaluation further shows improved fluency, with particularly strong results for the extremely low-resource Acehnese and Hitu. 3. Through extensive analyses, we examine when and why vocabulary-guided generation works, studying the impact of vocabulary quality, reasoning versus non-reasoning generation, and increasing generation volume. Our results highlight vocabulary quality as a key consideration and show whether gains in lexical diversity persist as synthetic data are generated at larger scale.
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献有三个方面: 1. 我们采用了一个无培训框架,利用LLM推理,从人文词汇和少量人文实例中以低资源语言生成文本。 我们的框架从Zipfian采样中调整,使模型暴露在一代人中广泛而自然的词汇分布中. 2. 我们的框架跨越不同水平的可用资源的六种语文,不断改进词汇的多样性,并比实际基线减少非目标生成。 人类评价还表明,流利程度有所提高,对亚齐和希图资源极其低的亚齐和希图而言,结果尤其显著。 3. 我们通过广泛分析,审查词汇指导生成工作的时间和原因,研究词汇质量的影响、推理与非理性生成以及增加生成量。 我们的成果强调词汇质量是一个关键考虑因素,并表明随着合成数据在更大范围内生成,词汇多样性方面的进步是否继续存在。

blocks.en: 2 Related Works
blocks.zh: 2 相关工程

blocks.en:
Synthetic data has long been used to supplement scarce human-written data in NLP ( Feng et al., 2021 ) . Early augmentation methods typically transform existing examples through operations such as synonym replacement, random insertion and deletion, and word swapping ( Wei and Zou, 2019 ; Karimi et al., 2021 ) .
The emergence of LLMs has enabled a shift toward generating new synthetic text at scale, with applications ranging from augmenting pretraining corpora ( Doshi et al., 2024 ; Zhu et al., 2026 ) to constructing post-training resources such as instruction-tuning data ( Wang et al., 2023 ) . Despite their strong generation capabilities, LLMs tend to produce text with lower lexical diversity than human-written data ( Guo et al., 2024 ; Kambhatla et al., 2025 ) .
This limitation is particularly relevant to our goal of expanding the lexical coverage of languages with limited textual resources. Therefore, we treat lexical diversity, alongside fluency, as a central dimension of synthetic text quality.
blocks.zh:
NLP中长期使用合成数据来补充稀缺的人类书面数据(Feng等人,2021年). 早期增强方法一般通过同义词替换,随机插入和删除,词交换等操作来改变现有实例(Wei and Zou, 2019;Karimi等人, 2021).
有限责任公司(LLMS)的出现使得人们能够转向大规模生成新的合成文本,其应用范围从增强预训公司(Doshi等人,2024年;Zhu等人,2026年)到构建培训后资源,如教学调试数据(Wang等人,2023年)。 尽管LLMS具有很强的生成能力,但其生成的文字多样性往往低于人类书面数据(Guo等人,2024年;Kambhatla等人,2025年)。
这一限制与我们扩大文字资源有限的语言的词汇范围的目标特别相关。 因此,我们把语言多样性和流利性作为合成文本质量的一个核心层面。

blocks.en:
Synthetic text generation is particularly challenging for low-resource languages, where LLMs have limited linguistic knowledge. Generation quality tends to deteriorate as language resources decrease ( Bafna et al., 2025 ) , and models may drift into higher-resource languages when generating underrepresented ones ( Marchisio et al., 2024 ) . Nevertheless, LLM-generated data have been explored for low-resource applications ranging from question answering to story generation ( Namboori et al., 2023 ; Cegin et al., 2025 ; Pranida et al., 2025 ) , with target-language demonstrations shown to improve their utility ( Anikina et al., 2025 ) . These approaches, however, largely rely on linguistic knowledge already encoded in the LLM. Our work instead asks whether LLMs can generate fluent and lexically diverse text with minimal off-target generation in extremely underrepresented languages, including languages not seen during LLM pretraining,
where we leverage LLM reasoning to combine with external lexical knowledge to provide additional linguistic information at inference time.
blocks.zh:
合成文本生成对于低资源语言尤其具有挑战性,因为LLMs语言知识有限. 随着语言资源的减少,生成质量往往会恶化(Bafna等人,2025年),当产生代表性不足的语言时,模型可能会转向资源较高的语言(Marchisio等人,2024年)。 尽管如此,还是为低资源应用(Namboori等人,2023年;Cegin等人,2025年;Pranida等人,2025年)探索了LLM生成的数据,显示目标语言演示提高了它们的效用(Anikina等人,2025年)。 然而,这些方法主要依靠已在LLM中编码的语言知识. 相反,我们的工作问LLM能否以极低代表性语言,包括LLM预训期间所未见的语言,生成流利和符合逻辑的多样文本,并尽量减少非目标生成,
我们利用LLM推理 与外部的词汇学知识相结合 在推断时间提供额外的语言信息

blocks.en:
Human-curated lexical resources, including dictionaries, bilingual lexicons, and word lists, cover substantially more languages than commonly available text corpora ( Wang et al., 2022 ) . Prior work has leveraged these resources for lexical augmentation, word-for-word data synthesis, and machine translation ( Feng et al., 2021 ; Wang et al., 2022 ; Peng et al., 2020 ) . Recent studies further show that providing dictionaries or grammatical resources in context can help LLMs translate languages scarcely represented in pretraining ( Tanzer et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) . These approaches, however, primarily focus on translation.
Closest to our work, Yong et al. (2024) condition LLMs on bilingual lexicons to generate task-specific data, which are subsequently translated word by word into the target language. In contrast, we study open-ended generation directly in the target language.
We use human-curated vocabularies as lexical knowledge and a few human-written exemplars as syntactic guidance, requiring the LLM to compose new text rather than translate or modify existing sentences.
blocks.zh:
包括词典、双语词典和词表在内的人文精准的词汇资源,涵盖的语言远远多于常用文本corpora(Wang等人,2022年). 先前的工作利用这些资源进行词汇扩充、字对字数据综合和机器翻译(冯等人,2021年;王等人,2022年;彭等人,2020年)。 最近的研究进一步表明,在语境中提供词典或语法资源可以帮助LLMs翻译在预训中几乎没有体现的语言(Tanzer等人,2024年;张等人,2024年). 然而,这些办法主要侧重于翻译。
最贴近我们的工作,勇等. (2024)在双语词典上设定LLMs的条件,以生成任务特定数据,这些数据随后逐字翻译为目标语言. 相比之下,我们直接用目标语言研究不限成员名额的一代。
我们使用人类精准的词汇作为词汇学知识,并使用几个人类书写的例子作为综合指导,要求LLM来编写新的文本,而不是翻译或修改现有的句子.

blocks.en: 3 Methodology
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: We illustrate our training-free, vocabulary-guided synthetic text generation pipeline in Figure 1 . The pipeline consists of four stages: (1) collecting human-curated dictionaries and word-frequency information for each target language, (2) collecting a small set of human-written exemplars in sentences and paragraphs, (3) sampling candidate words according to their frequency distribution, and (4) constructing the generation prompt from the sampled words and exemplars.
blocks.zh: 我们用图1来说明我们的无培训、词汇指导的合成文本生成管道。 管道由四个阶段组成:(1)收集每种目标语言的人语精密词典和词频信息,(2)收集句子和段落中一小组人语书写实例,(3)根据其频率分布对候选词进行取样,(4)从样本词和实例中构建生成提示.

blocks.en:
We first collect a human-curated dictionary 𝒟 \mathcal{D} for each target language and standardize its entries into a common format. Each entry w ∈ 𝒟 w\in\mathcal{D} consists of a target-language word, its English equivalent en ⁡ ( w ) \mathrm{en}(w) , an English definition, a part-of-speech (POS) tag, and, when available, an example sentence illustrating its usage.
Because the available resources differ substantially across languages and formats, we use language-specific procedures to construct the dictionaries. Appendix A describes the data sources and processing procedures and reports the number of entries collected for each language (Table 5 ).

blocks.en: We next estimate how frequently each dictionary word is likely to occur in natural text. Direct frequency estimates are unavailable or unreliable for many of our target languages, particularly the extremely low-resource ones. We therefore derive approximate frequencies from English using the Dictionary Word Frequency dataset, 2 2 2 A preprocessed dataset based on Google Books Ngram . which provides unigram counts from Google Books. Each entry w w is assigned the frequency f ⁡ ( w ) f(w) of its English equivalent en ⁡ ( w ) \mathrm{en}(w) . Entries whose English equivalent has no frequency are excluded from frequency-based sampling, and the remaining entries form the vocabulary 𝒱 ⊆ 𝒟 \mathcal{V}\subseteq\mathcal{D} . We rank the entries of 𝒱 \mathcal{V} from highest to lowest f ⁡ ( w ) f(w) and denote the rank of entry w w by r ⁡ ( w ) r(w) , so that r ⁡ ( w ) = 1 r(w)=1 for the most frequent entry. The resulting distribution is heavy-tailed, with a small number of highly frequent words and a long tail of less frequent words, consistent with Zipf’s law. We use this ranking for word-candidate sampling in Stage 3.

blocks.en: In parallel, we collect a small set of human-written exemplars to provide syntactic and contextual guidance for generation ( Anikina et al., 2025 ) . For each language (Section 4 ), we recruit one native-speaker annotator. Recruiting native speakers is particularly challenging for the extremely low-resource languages in our study. To ensure the quality of the exemplars, we apply strict eligibility criteria: annotators must have at least a senior high school education, must have lived for at least 10 years in a community where the target language is spoken, and must have at least one parent who speaks the language. Each annotator writes 40 sentences and 5 paragraphs. The sentences cover four target lengths (5, 10, 15, and 20 words), with 10 sentences per length. Each paragraph contains at least three sentences and at least 25 words. We denote the resulting pool of exemplars by ℰ \mathcal{E} . Each exemplar e ∈ ℰ e\in\mathcal{E} consists of a target-language text, its English translation, and the set of dictionary entries 𝒟 ⁡ ( e ) ⊆ 𝒟 \mathcal{D}(e)\subseteq\mathcal{D} used to compose it, following the schema of Stage 1. These exemplars show how dictionary entries are composed naturally in context, and we use them as few-shot guidance during generation. Appendix B describes the annotation procedure in detail.

blocks.en: To generate each synthetic sentence or paragraph, we provide the LLM with two inputs: s s few-shot exemplars and k k word candidates. The exemplars provide syntactic and contextual guidance, while the word candidates encourage lexical diversity. Sampling uniformly from the vocabulary, however, would overrepresent rare words and underrepresent common ones, including function words. We therefore sample the word candidates using the frequency estimates from Stage 1, so that they better reflect natural patterns of word usage.
blocks.zh: 为了生成每个合成句子或段落,我们向LLM提供了两个输入:s 几个shot examplars and k k word contents. 实例提供了综合和背景指导,而考生一词则鼓励词汇多样性. 然而,从词汇中统一取样,将过度代表稀有的词,而不足代表常见的词,包括函数词。 因此,我们利用第一阶段的频率估计对候选词进行抽样,以便更好地反映字数使用的自然规律。

blocks.en: 4.1 Configurations
blocks.zh: 4.1 配置

blocks.en: We conduct the experiment with 6 languages, 3 models, 2 thinking modes, 3 prompting strategies, and 5 text lengths, which results in a total of 540 combinations of configurations. We generate 100 outputs for each combination, yielding a total of 54,000 outputs. The configurations are as follows.
blocks.zh: 我们用6种语言,3种模型,2种思维模式,3种提示策略,5种文字长度进行实验,结果组合组合共540种. 我们为每种组合产生100项产出,共产生54 000项产出。 配置如下.

blocks.en: We experiment with six Southeast Asian languages spanning different levels of resource availability: Indonesian and Vietnamese as medium-resource languages, Javanese and Minangkabau as low-resource languages, and Acehnese and Hitu as extremely low-resource languages.
blocks.zh: 我们试验了6种东南亚语言,涵盖不同资源水平:印度尼西亚语和越南语作为中资源语言,爪哇语和米南卡包语作为低资源语言,亚齐语和希图语作为极低资源语言。

blocks.en: We evaluate three LLMs: Gemini 3.5 Flash ( Google, 2026 ) , Claude Haiku 4.5 ( Anthropic, 2025 ) , and GPT-5.4 Mini ( OpenAI, 2026 ) . Each model is evaluated with reasoning enabled and disabled, resulting in six configurations. We initially also considered open-weight models, including Llama 3.3 70B ( Grattafiori et al., 2024 ; Meta AI, 2024 ) and Qwen2.5 72B ( Yang et al., 2024 ) . However, preliminary evaluation showed substantially lower fluency, particularly for low-resource languages. Because our primary fluency evaluation requires native-speaker judgments, we exclude these models from the full evaluation and focus our annotation budget on the stronger model configurations.
blocks.zh: 我们评价三个LLMs:双子座3.5 Flash(Google,2026年),Claude Haiku 4.5(Anthropic,2025年),和GPT-5.4 Mini(OpenAI,2026年). 每个模型都经过了推理的启用和禁用评估,结果产生了6个配置. 我们最初也考虑过开放重量型号,包括Llama 3.3 70B(Grattafiori等人,2024年;Meta AI,2024年)和Quen2.5 72B(Yang等人,2024年). 然而,初步评价表明,流利程度低得多,特别是对于低资源语言而言。 因为我们的初级流利性评价需要本地语言的判断,我们将这些模型排除在全面评价之外,并将我们的注释预算集中在更强大的模型配置上.

blocks.en: We compare three prompting strategies that differ in the amount of information provided to the LLM. The first two serve as baselines, while the third is the strategy used in our method: 1. Topic-Conditioned Zero-Shot Prompt (Zero-shot): This prompt only instructs the model to generate text in the target language about a given topic (see the full prompt in Appendix D ). 2. Few-Shot Exemplars Only Prompt (Few-shot): This prompt adds human-written exemplars of the target length to the instruction (see the full prompt in Appendix E ). 3. Few-Shot Exemplars and Word Candidates Prompt (Ours): This prompt adds both human-written exemplars of the target length and word candidates sampled from the dictionary to the instruction, as discussed in Section 3 (see the full prompt in Appendix F ).
blocks.zh: 我们比较了向LLM提供的信息数量不同的三个激励战略。 前两项是基线,第三项是我们方法中使用的战略: 1. 专题条件 零热速射(零射) : 这个提示只指示模型以特定主题的目标语言生成文本(见附录D中的完整提示). 2. " 极少数实例 " : 这个提示为指示添加了目标长度的人类书面实例(见附录E中的完整提示). 3. 少数热门实例和言语候选人(我们的): 如第3节所讨论(见附录F的完整提示),这一提示将标的长度的人文示例和从字典中抽取的字词候选人都添加到指令中。

blocks.en: We generate texts at five sequence lengths: sentences of 5, 10, 15, and 20 words, and paragraphs consisting of 3 sentences and 25 words. This setup lets us test whether the LLM can generate text across a range of lengths.

blocks.en: 4.2 Evaluation Metrics.
blocks.zh: 4.2 评价计量。

blocks.en: We evaluate the generated outputs along three dimensions: fluency, off-target rate, and lexical diversity. We compute each score at the level of a configuration.
blocks.zh: 我们从三个方面评价所产生的产出:流畅度、非目标率和词汇多样性。 我们按配置水平计算每个分数。

blocks.en: We conduct a human evaluation to assess the fluency of the generated texts. Due to annotation costs, we evaluate a subset of outputs covering three models with only thinking mode enabled, three prompting strategies, and three text lengths (5-word sentences, 15-word sentences, and paragraphs), with 30 texts per configuration, resulting in 810 texts per language. Each language is annotated by two annotators. They see only the generated texts, presented in a different random order for each annotator, and complete the annotation independently. They rate each text on a 1–5 scale following our annotation guidelines (see Appendix G ), where a higher score indicates a more fluent and natural text. We measure inter-annotator agreement using Pearson and Spearman correlations and observe moderate agreement between the two annotators (see Table 1 ). The final fluency score for each text is the average of the two annotators’ ratings.
blocks.zh: 我们进行了一次人文评估,以评估所生成文本的流畅度。 由于注释费用,我们评价了一组产出,包括三个模式,只允许思维模式,三个提示策略,以及三个文本长度(5个句子,15个句子,和段落),每个配置有30个文本,结果每个语言有810个文本. 每种语言都由两个注释员作注释. 他们只看到生成的文本,以不同的随机顺序为每个注释者呈现,独立完成注释. 他们按照我们的说明准则(见附录G),以1比5的比例对每个文本进行评分,其中较高的分数表明文字更流畅和自然。 我们使用皮尔逊和斯皮尔曼的相互关系来测量注释者之间的协议,并观察两个注释者之间的温和协议(见表1)。 每个文本的最终流利分数是两个注释者评分的平均值.

blocks.en: We measure off-target rate as the proportion of words in a generated text that do not appear in the target-language dictionary. This metric evaluates a model’s tendency to produce text outside the desired language, reflecting language confusion ( Marchisio et al., 2024 ) or complete failure to produce that language. Scores range from 0 to 1, where 1 means that none of the generated text belongs to the target language, so higher values indicate greater language confusion. We score each output independently and average the scores over each configuration.

blocks.en: 5 Results
blocks.zh: 5 结果

blocks.en: Table 2 reports the results for each language and prompt, averaged across all evaluated models. Results for each individual model and thinking mode are reported in Appendix J (Table 8 ). We organize the discussion around the evaluation metrics described in Section 4.2 .
blocks.zh: 表2报告每种语文的结果,以及所有评价模型的迅速平均结果。 附录J(表8)报告了每个模型和思维模式的结果。 我们围绕第4.2节所述的评价指标组织讨论。

blocks.en: Our prompt achieves the highest fluency for Minangkabau, Acehnese, and Hitu at every text length, exceeding the best baseline by an average of 0.33, 0.69, and 0.79 points, respectively. The margin grows as resource availability decreases and is largest for the extremely low-resource languages, where baseline fluency drops sharply (e.g., 1.61–1.79 for zero-shot in Hitu). For Indonesian, all prompts score close to the maximum, with few-shot marginally ahead. For Vietnamese and Javanese, however, our prompt trails both baselines, particularly for Vietnamese paragraphs (3.54 vs. 4.72 for zero-shot). We hypothesize that this stems from the quality of the underlying dictionaries: inaccurate or poorly matched entries are passed directly to the model, whereas the baselines rely only on its own knowledge. We examine this hypothesis in Section 6 . Finally, fluency generally decreases as texts get longer.
blocks.zh: 我们迅速使Minangkabau、Azinese和Hitu在每一文本长度上都达到最高流利,分别超过最佳基线0.33、0.69和0.79点。 随着资源供应的减少,差值增加,对于资源极其低的语文而言,幅度最大,因为基线流利程度急剧下降(例如,Hitu的零射线为1.61-1.79)。 对于印尼人来说,所有提示的得分都接近最高点,只有几分领先。 然而,对越南和爪哇内斯来说,我们迅速追踪了这两个基线,特别是越南段落(3.54和4.72)的零射线。 我们假设,这来源于基本词典的质量:不准确或不匹配的条目直接传递给模型,而基线则只依靠其自身的知识. 我们在第6节中审查了这个假设。 最后,随着文本的延长,流畅度普遍下降。

blocks.en: Our prompt achieves the lowest off-target rate in all six languages. For both baselines, the rate rises steadily as resource availability decreases: with zero-shot prompting, it grows from 0.015–0.028 for the medium-resource languages to 0.836 for Hitu, where most generated words are not in the target language. Our prompt breaks this pattern, keeping the rate at or below 0.090 for every language. The reductions are therefore largest for the extremely low-resource languages, from 0.609 with few-shot prompting to 0.060 for Hitu and from 0.315 to 0.064 for Acehnese. For Indonesian and Vietnamese, all prompts produce very few off-target words, with differences of at most 0.014.
blocks.zh: 我们迅速在所有六种语言中实现最低的离目标率。 在这两种基线中,随着资源供应量的减少,增长率稳步上升:随着零射线的提示,中资源语言从0.015-0.028增加到了希图语的0.836,而希图语中大多数生成的词不是目标语言。 我们迅速打破这种模式,使每种语言的费率保持在0.090或以下。 因此,极低资源语言的减少幅度最大,Hitu的减少幅度从0.609, 少发速射的减少幅度从0.060,亚齐的减少幅度从0.315, 0.064。 对于印度尼西亚语和越南语来说,所有提示都产生极少的离目标词,差异最多为0.014.

blocks.en: Our prompt yields the highest lexical diversity for every language and text length. The gains hold even for the medium-resource languages, where off-target words are rare: for Indonesian, our prompt scores 0.72–0.87 against 0.43–0.61 for the baselines, indicating that the word candidates broaden the vocabulary rather than only reducing off-target words. The gap widens as resource availability decreases. For Hitu, the baselines score below 0.09 at every length because their outputs are largely off-target and repetitive, whereas our prompt scores 0.51–0.75, an average improvement of 0.57 over few-shot prompting. For our prompt, lexical diversity decreases steadily with text length in every language and is lowest for paragraphs, partly because longer texts inevitably repeat common words.
blocks.zh: 我们的迅速为每种语言和文本长度产生最高的语法多样性。 对印尼人来说, 我们的快速得分是0. 72–0. 87, 而基线是0. 43–0. 61, 这表明候选词拓宽了词汇, 随着资源供应的减少,差距不断扩大。 对希图来说,基线的得分每长都低于0.09,因为其产出大多是非目标且重复的,而我们的迅速得分是0.51-0.75,平均比几发快0.57。 对我们来说,词汇的多样性随每种语文的文本长度而逐渐减少,对于段落来说最低,部分原因是较长的文本不可避免地重复了共同的词语。

blocks.en: 6 Analysis
blocks.zh: 6 分析

blocks.en: Our method scores below the baselines in fluency for Vietnamese and Javanese. To investigate these cases, we asked the annotators to examine the generated texts and the vocabulary entries provided to the model. Their feedback suggests that dictionary quality plays an important role. For Vietnamese, some dictionary entries were valid but uncommon in everyday usage, while more familiar alternatives were missing. As a result, semantically correct generations could still sound unnatural to native speakers. For Javanese, the dictionary primarily represents the Yogyakarta variety, whereas our annotator speaks Javanese with Arekan dialect. This mismatch led to unfamiliar vocabulary appearing in the generated text, reducing perceived fluency despite the words being valid dictionary entries. These observations highlight an important practical consideration for vocabulary-guided generation: the dictionary should be validated for both lexical coverage and alignment with the target language variety before large-scale generation. In particular, commonly used words should be adequately represented, and the lexical resource should match the variety spoken by the intended users.
blocks.zh: 我们的方法在越南语和爪哇语的流利度低于基线。 为了调查这些案件,我们请注释员审查生成的文本和提供给模型的词汇条目。 他们的反馈表明,词典质量发挥着重要作用. 对越南人来说,一些字典条目是有效的,但在日常使用中并不常见,同时缺少更熟悉的替代词. 因此,对讲母语的人来说,模棱两可的几代人仍然听起来不自然。 对于Javanese来说,字典主要代表日惹品种,而我们的注释员用Arekan方言说Javanese. 这种不匹配导致生成的文本中出现的不熟悉词汇,减少了人们所认为的流利,尽管这些词是有效的词典条目. 这些意见突出了词汇制导生成的重要实际考虑:字典在大规模生成之前,应同时验证词典的词典涵盖范围,并与目标语言品种保持一致. 特别是,常用的词应该得到充分的体现,词汇资源应该与预期使用者所说的种类相匹配。

The judge’s reliability varies across languages, as shown in Table 3 . Spearman’s correlation is moderate for most languages, strongest for Acehnese (0.69), and weakest for Hitu (0.15), suggesting that the judge’s rankings of Hitu texts align poorly with human judgments of fluency. MAE and bias show a clearer pattern.
For Indonesian, the judge’s scores show the closest agreement with human ratings, with the lowest MAE (0.12) and a near-zero bias (-0.04). For the remaining languages, the MAE is generally higher, and the bias is consistently positive, indicating that the judge tends to assign higher scores than the human. This overestimation is particularly pronounced for Minangkabau (+0.60) and Acehnese (+0.58), and greatest for Hitu, which also has the highest MAE (+1.19).

如表3所示,法官的可靠性因语言而异。 Spearman的关联性对于大多数语言来说是温和的,对亚齐语(0.69)最强,对希图语(0.15)最弱,这表明法官对希图语的排名与人类对流利的判断不一致. MAE和偏差显示出更明确的模式.
对于印尼人来说,评委的分数最接近人类的评分,最低的MAE(0.12)和接近零的偏差(-0.04). 对其余语言来说,MAE一般更高,偏差始终是正面的,表明裁判倾向于分配比人类更高的分数. 这种高估尤其突出的是Minangkabau(+0.60)和亚齐(+0.58),而Hitu(也拥有最高的MAE(+1.19)。

blocks.en: Overall, the results show that the judge’s agreement with human annotators varies across languages. While its fluency rankings align relatively well with human judgments for Acehnese, it tends to assign higher scores than human annotators and has larger scoring errors for several lower-resource languages. Therefore, LLM-as-a-judge should be used with caution for fluency evaluation in these languages and should not be considered a substitute for human evaluation.
blocks.zh: 总的来说,结果显示,法官与人类注释员的协议因语言而异。 虽然其流利的排名与亚齐语的人类判断相对一致,但往往比人类的注释者获得更高的分数,一些资源较少的语言的分数错误较大. 因此,应谨慎使用作为法官的LLM来进行这些语言的流利评价,而不应被视为人类评价的替代品。

blocks.en: We investigate whether generating larger volumes of text leads to reduced lexical diversity and whether our prompt mitigates this effect compared with the baselines. We run this stress test experiment in Minangkabau and Hitu, generating up to 1,000 five-word sentences for each prompting strategy using Gemini 3.5 Flash with thinking mode enabled. We compute the percentage of unique valid n-grams among those observed in the first N N sentences, where N = 100,200 , … , 1000 N=100,200,\ldots,1000 .
blocks.zh: 我们调查产生更多文本是否导致语法多样性的减少,以及我们是否与基线相比迅速减轻这种影响。 我们在Minangkabau和Hitu进行压力测试实验, 使用双子座3.5 Flash, 并启用思维模式, 我们计算在N N 第一句中观察到的独特有效正方克的百分比,其中N = 100 200,...,1000 N = 100 200,\ldots 100。

blocks.en: Figures 2 and 3 show that this percentage decreases as more sentences are generated across all prompting strategies, which is expected as repeated n-grams accumulate. In Minangkabau, the zero-shot and few-shot scores are 0.32 and 0.36 at 100 sentences and drop to between 0.14 and 0.15 at 1,000 sentences. The same pattern holds in Hitu, where the zero-shot and few-shot scores fall from 0.16 and 0.05 to 0.09 and 0.04, respectively. However, our prompt consistently maintains a higher percentage than the baselines in both languages, suggesting that it better preserves lexical diversity as generation volume increases.
blocks.zh: 图2和图3显示,随着所有促动战略中产生更多句子,这一百分比会下降,预计随着重复的正克累积。 在Minangkabau中,零射和数射的分数在100句下为0.32分和0.36分,在1000句下降至0.14至0.15分. 同样的模式在希图也存在,该地的零射和少射的分数分别从0.16和0.05下降到0.09和0.04. 然而,我们的迅速性始终保持高于两种语文的基线的百分比,这表明随着发电量的增加,它更好地维护了词汇的多样性。

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: We introduced a training-free framework that leverages human-curated vocabularies, human-written exemplars, and LLM reasoning to generate synthetic text in low-resource languages. Across six languages, our framework produces more lexically diverse text with fewer off-target words than the baselines, while improving fluency particularly for the extremely low-resource Acehnese and Hitu. These results show the potential of human-curated vocabularies for bootstrapping synthetic text corpora where existing text resources are limited.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了一个免费培训框架,利用人语词汇、人文实例和LLM推理,以低资源语言生成合成文本。 在六种语言中,我们的框架产生了更具逻辑多样性的文本,其非目标字比基线要少,同时提高流利度,特别是对于资源极低的亚齐和希图。 这些结果表明,在现有文本资源有限的地方,人语化词汇有可能将合成文本拼凑在一起。

blocks.en: Our analysis also highlights important practical considerations. Dictionary quality and alignment with the target language variety can substantially affect generation quality, making vocabulary validation important before large-scale generation. The framework also requires additional input tokens for word candidates and exemplars, creating a trade-off between generation quality and cost. Future work should extend the framework to more low-resource languages and investigate whether the resulting synthetic corpora improve LLM pretraining and post-training.
blocks.zh: 我们的分析还突出了重要的实际考虑。 词典质量和与目标语言品种的配合会严重影响生成质量,使得词汇验证在大规模生成之前很重要. 该框架还需要文字候选人和实例的额外输入符号,从而在生成质量和成本之间形成一种权衡。 今后的工作应当将该框架扩大到资源更低的语言,并调查由此产生的合成公司是否改进了LLM预训和后培训。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our experiments cover six Southeast Asian languages, five of which are Austronesian and all written in Latin script. Five are spoken in Indonesia and share considerable lexical material with Indonesian, a setting that is likely to favor positive transfer. We therefore cannot claim that the framework generalizes to non-Latin scripts or to agglutinative or polysynthetic morphology.
We further describe Hitu as unseen during pretraining, but the training corpora of the three commercial models we use are not public, so this characterization is inferred from model behavior rather than established, as illustrated in Appendix H .
blocks.zh:
我们的实验涵盖6种东南亚语言,其中5种是奥斯特罗尼西亚语,全部用拉丁字母书写. 在印度尼西亚讲了五种语言,与印度尼西亚人分享了大量的词汇材料,这种背景可能有利于积极转让。 因此,我们不能声称,框架一般适用于非拉丁文文字或阳性或多合成形态。
我们进一步将Hitu描述为在预训期间所未见的,但是我们使用的三种商业模型的训练公司并不公开,因此这种定性是从模型行为推断出来的,而不是由建立起来的,如附录H所示.

blocks.en: As our experiments are extensive, generating 54,000 texts made broad model coverage too costly, so we limit our study to three proprietary models accessed through commercial APIs, all from the economy tier of their respective families. Our findings are therefore restricted to these models, which are the latest versions of these model families at the time of our experiments. It remains unclear whether the gains hold for larger or more recent models, which may already encode more of these languages.
blocks.zh: 由于我们的实验范围很广,生成54,000个文本使得广泛的模型覆盖成本太高,因此我们的研究仅限于通过商业API获取的三种专有模型,它们都来自各自家庭的经济层面. 因此,我们的发现仅限于这些模型,这些模型是我们实验时这些模型家族的最新版本. 目前仍然不清楚的是,收益是用于更大或更近期的模型,这些模型可能已经编码了更多的这些语言。

blocks.en: Furthermore, we evaluate the fluency, off-target rate, and lexical diversity of the generated text, but we have not trained or fine-tuned any model on the resulting data. With the quality gains in fluency and lexical diversity reported in Table 2 , we see this as a promising direction for future work: testing whether our method benefits downstream models, particularly for LRLs.
blocks.zh: 此外,我们评价生成的文本的流利性、非目标率和词汇多样性,但我们没有就由此产生的数据培训或微调任何模型。 随着表2所报告的流利性和语言多样性的质量提高,我们认为这是未来工作的一个有希望的方向:测试我们的方法是否有利于下游模式,特别是对于长效半衰期。

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en: This work involved native speakers of the six target languages, who wrote the few-shot exemplars (Appendix B ) and rated the fluency of the generated texts (Appendix G ). Before agreeing to participate, annotators were informed of the purpose of the study, the expected workload, and the intended research use of their contributions. They were paid above the regional minimum wage in Indonesia and Vietnam and were free to withdraw at any point. No personal or sensitive information was collected, and none appears in our released materials. The Javanese, Minangkabau, Hitu, and Acehnese dictionaries are published by the Indonesian Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, and the Indonesian and Vietnamese resources are distributed under Apache-2.0 and MIT licences; we use all resources for non-commercial academic research only and cite them in full (Appendix A ).

blocks.en: Appendix B Few-Shot Exemplar Creation Procedure
blocks.zh: 附录B

blocks.en: We assigned one native-speaker annotator to each target language. Each annotator is a native speaker of or fluent in the target local language and has lived in the region where the language is spoken for a period of time.
blocks.zh: 我们为每种目标语言指派了一名当地语言注释员。 每个注释员是目标当地语言的母语人或流利语言人,在讲该语言的地区居住了一段时间.

blocks.en: The exemplar creation process began with the development of annotation guidelines. Before commencing the task, annotators were asked to read the guidelines carefully and were encouraged to raise any questions or seek clarification about aspects they found unclear.
blocks.zh: 示范创建过程始于制定注释指南. 在开始这项工作之前,请注释员仔细阅读准则,并鼓励他们提出任何问题或要求澄清他们认为不明确的方面。

blocks.en: Each annotator was provided with a separate Google Sheets document to record the exemplars they created, along with the corresponding dictionary dataset to facilitate the selection of candidate words. The dictionary entries provided lexical information, including the word, part of speech, English definition, and example sentence. Annotators were instructed to use words from the provided dictionary dataset whenever possible when constructing the exemplars. A Jupyter Notebook was also provided to assist annotators in searching relevant dictionary entries. Figure 4 presents the guidelines.
blocks.zh: 每个注释员都得到了一个单独的Google Sheets文档,以记录他们创建的示例,以及相应的词典数据集,以便于选择候选词. 该词典条目提供了词汇信息,包括词,语音的一部分,英语定义,以及示例句子. 指示注释者在构建实例时尽可能使用所提供的词典数据集中的单词. 还提供了一本Jupyter Notebook,以协助注释员搜索相关的词典条目。 图4列出了准则。

blocks.en:
Exemplar Creation Guidelines The annotation task consists of creating 40 sentences and 5 paragraphs in the
target language. The sentences should be distributed as follows: • 10 sentences of approximately 5 words each; • 10 sentences of approximately 10 words each; • 10 sentences of approximately 15 words each; • 10 sentences of approximately 20 words each; and • 5 paragraphs, with each paragraph containing at least 3 sentences
and at least 25 words. Small variations in sentence length are acceptable as long as the sentence
remains natural. For example, a target of 5 words corresponds approximately
to 4–6 words, while a target of 10 words corresponds approximately to
9–11 words. For each exemplar, annotators should fill the following fields: • sentence : the sentence or paragraph written in the target
language; • translation : the English translation of the sentence or
paragraph; and • words_candidates : the dictionary entries corresponding
to the words used to construct the sentence or paragraph. For the words_candidates field, annotators should identify the
dictionary entry corresponding to each word used in the sentence whenever
possible. Dictionary entries are provided in the following format: word | pos | definition | example where word is the word in the target language, pos is its
part of speech, definition is its English definition, and example is an example sentence when available. Annotators should use words from the provided dictionary dataset whenever possible. If an additional word is needed to produce a natural and
grammatically correct sentence but is not available in the dictionary
dataset, the annotator may introduce it as a new word candidate. The new
word should also be recorded using the same dictionary entry format.

blocks.en: As a native speaker of [TARGET_LANGUAGE] , your task is to rate the fluency of each given text on a 1–5 Likert scale. Scoring Rubric: 1. Very Poor: The text is largely unintelligible due to severe grammatical errors, broken syntax, or nonsensical word order. The intended meaning is difficult or impossible to determine. This score also applies if the text is an automated error response or is written in another language. 2. Poor: The intended meaning is mostly recoverable, but frequent grammatical errors, incorrect word order, or unnatural phrasing make the text difficult to read. 3. Fair: The meaning is clear, but the text contains some grammatical errors or awkward constructions that reduce its naturalness. 4. Good: The text is grammatically correct and easy to understand, with only minor stylistic awkwardness or slightly unnatural wording. 5. Excellent: The text is completely fluent, natural, and reads as if written by a proficient native speaker. Examples: 1. Very Poor: “Yesterday market she because apples the quickly and was.” 2. Poor: “She go market yesterday buy apples for she family.” 3. Fair: “She went to market yesterday for buying apples for her family.” 4. Good: “She went to the market yesterday to buy apples for her family.” 5. Excellent: “She went to the market yesterday to buy fresh apples for her family, since they had run out at home.”
blocks.zh: 作为[TARGET_LANGUAGE]的母语,你的任务是将每个文本的流利度评分为1至5等号。 校对 Rubric : 1. 赤贫: 由于语法错误严重,语法断裂,或词序不敏感,文字基本上无法理解. 意图的含义很难或不可能确定。 如果文字是自动错误反应或者用另一种语言写成,这个分数也适用. 2. 穷:原意大多可以恢复,但经常出现语法错误,词序不正确,或措辞不自然,使得文本难以阅读. 3. 公平: 其含义是明确的,但文本中包含了一些语法错误或尴尬的构造,降低了其自然性. 4. 不错: 文字在语法上是正确的,易于理解,只有轻微的风格尴尬或略显不自然的措辞. 5. 优秀: 文字完全流利,自然,读起来就像一位熟练的本地演说家写的一样. 实例: 1. 十分贫穷:“昨天她上市,因为苹果很快就上市了。 ” “她昨天去市场买苹果, 3. 博览会:“她昨天去市场买苹果给家人。” 4. Good:“她昨天去市场为家人买苹果。” 5. 极好: " 她昨天去市场为家人购买新鲜苹果,因为家里的苹果已经用完。 “
